policy.text:
# Internal Policy: General Dispute Handling Process

**Applies to:** Any complaint not governed more specifically by another policy in this set (i.e., the default process).

## Standard process
1. **Acknowledge** receipt within 3 business days.
2. **Investigate** — compare the customer's claim against account and transaction records.
3. **Classify** the outcome as one of: confirmed (company error), not confirmed (no error found), partially confirmed (mixed), or unable to verify (insufficient data).
4. **Respond** in writing within 15 calendar days of receipt (consistent with standard regulatory complaint-handling expectations), addressing every distinct allegation raised in the complaint individually — a response that addresses only the primary complaint and ignores a secondary request is incomplete.
5. **Close** the case with a documented root-cause category for internal trend reporting.

## What counts as a complete response
- Every distinct factual allegation is addressed (confirmed, not confirmed, or unable to verify).
- Every distinct request the customer made is addressed (a refund request and an account-closure request in the same complaint both need a response, even if only one is granted).
- The response states a clear next step or outcome — never ends on an open-ended "we are looking into it" with no indication of what happens next, unless the case is genuinely still pending additional information.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state what was investigated and the outcome in plain language.
- May NOT close a case as "resolved" if any raised allegation was not actually addressed.

## Escalation trigger
Use the dedicated Escalation Criteria policy (document 09) for attorney/regulator/vulnerability triggers. This document covers only the baseline process for complaints that don't meet those triggers.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

draft.draft_text:
Thank you for telling us about the repeated phone calls over your payday loan debt. We understand how stressful this has been, especially when it makes you afraid to answer your own phone. We looked at each concern you raised.

**Number of calls:** The call log we reviewed shows 4 calls on March 30 and 5 calls on March 31, which matches what you described. It also shows a call on April 1 at 12:05 p.m. that was answered and lasted about 2 minutes.

**Calls before 8am:** Our records confirm calls at 7:41 a.m. on March 30 and at 7:55 a.m. on March 31.

**Your requests for mail-only contact:** We could not find a record of a mail-only request in your account notes or history. A request made directly to the collection agency might not appear in our records, so this does not mean you did not make one. The only mailed item we have is the collection notice dated March 2, which was sent before these calls. What was said on the April 1 call is not recorded.

**What happens next:** Your request to be contacted by mail only has been passed on for review, along with the call dates and times above. We cannot tell you the result or a date yet, and we will not promise an outcome before that review is complete.

If you can tell us when and how you asked for mail-only contact (for example, by phone or letter), or send any letters, texts, or voicemails, please do. You are welcome to send us more information at any time, and we will review it. You can reply to this message or call the number on your account.

Case reference: 20962593

draft.draft_text:
Thank you for telling us about the repeated phone calls from the collection agency on your payday loan debt. We understand how stressful it is to be afraid to pick up your own phone, and we looked carefully at what you described.

Here is what we found on each point:

1. Calls 4 to 5 times a day: Our call records confirm this. They show 4 calls on March 30, 2026 and 5 calls on March 31, 2026. A further call was answered on April 1, 2026 at 12:05.

2. Calls before 8am: Our records confirm this too. Calls were placed at 7:41am on March 30 and 7:55am on March 31.

3. The debt the calls are about: Our records show your payday loan account in collection, and a collection notice was mailed to you on March 2, 2026.

4. Your requests to be contacted by mail only: We could not confirm this. We found no record of a mail-only request in our account notes or history. A request made directly to the collection agency might not appear in our records. We also have no record of what was said on the April 1 call.

5. Your fear of answering the phone: We have noted what you shared about how these calls are affecting you.

Because we could not find a record of your mail-only request, we cannot confirm a mail-only contact preference on our side at this time. No other remedy has been approved on this complaint.

To help us look into this further, please reply to this message with when and how you asked to be contacted by mail only (for example, by phone or in writing), and who you spoke with if you remember. Copies of any letters or notes you kept would also help. You are welcome to send us anything further at any time, and we will review it.

Case reference: 20962593
